challengePass.reason: The outside-the-box pass favored a zero-new-dependency systemd transient-unit experiment and nsjail as the strongest mature comparator, but neither has been executed on the identical Ferrum process/service workload. Sandlock was specifically not promoted despite attractive performance because fresh unresolved security/correctness issues undermine the current proof gate.

nextExperiments: Run one deterministic Ferrum-owned process/service workload plain versus a strict systemd-run transient unit on a qualifying Linux host, recording effective security/resource properties, functional/evidence parity, denial behavior, cleanup, startup median/p95 and process identity.

If systemd-run is unavailable or materially incomplete, run the identical workload under nsjail 3.6 with read-only filesystem, isolated network and resource limits; compare against the same plain baseline.
Use sandboxec and landrun as lighter Landlock baselines only after the first full isolation comparator, and require machine-readable effective ABI/rights without silent degradation.
Revisit Sandlock only after its fresh AF_UNIX, Python mount parsing and destructive FFI fallback issues are resolved in a release; then rerun the identical fixture before any Ferrum integration.
Reserve gVisor, Kata and Firecracker for demonstrated strong-isolation needs rather than making VM/container infrastructure a default Ferrum dependency.
guardrails: No product code or supported target was changed this run.
No isolation feature will be advertised until a real runtime proves requested protections are active; missing capabilities must fail closed.
Existing unsandboxed process targets remain unchanged and available.
Isolation may not reduce test steps, evidence, diagnostics, fidelity, datasets, refresh rate or supported platform coverage.
Raw process logs, exit/signal identity, runtime/build identity and Ferrum evidence remain authoritative beside isolation summaries.
